notes: Three items queued, all three read. Two of them are the same article — the feed is a Bluesky account and it posted the Konstin obituary twice, under two bit.ly shortlinks that land on the same story.

coverage.note: This feed's titles are teaser sentences and its links are bit.ly shortlinks, so both headline and article URL were read off the article itself, per news/AGENTS.md. The obituary produced the false hit "100 Bay" from a photo caption dated in the byline block, and 63 Ellis Street is John's Grill's own address.

findings.description: Disney has signed a 76,000-square-foot lease at One Market Plaza, the 1.6-million-square-foot waterfront office complex, according to multiple sources the outlet confirmed the deal with; it follows the complex losing an anchor lease from Google last year, and departures by Visa and Autodesk ahead of expiring leases. The owner, Elecor Properties, announced 150,000 square feet of new leases over the summer. Elecor is an office platform created after Rithm Capital acquired the previous owner, Paramount Group, in 2025. The article names the complex only as "One Market Plaza" and "One Market" and prints no street number; the street number recorded here is that name's own, and the resolution below is what tests it against EAS.

citation.label: San Francisco Chronicle, “Exclusive: This S.F. office complex lost Google. Now it’s landing Disney,” 3 September 2026

raw.text: The 1.6 million-square-foot office complex at San Francisco's waterfront, which last year lost a major lease from anchor tenant Google, has signed Disney to a 76,000-square-foot lease.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 1 MARKET ST → parcel 3713006; sf-parcels has blklot 3713006 active, 1–1 MARKET; the 2025 roll records it as commercial office, built 1917.

raw.text: Another building in its portfolio, the 660,000-square-foot tower at 300 Mission St., is bumping its occupancy close to 87% after forging a new lease Hinge Health.

publish.note: The fact is solid and the address is unambiguous, but the entry is the headline and this headline is about One Market Plaza losing Google and landing Disney. Hanging it on 300 Mission's timeline would tell a reader something untrue about this tower. The Hinge Health lease is real news for this building and it needs its own story before it earns an entry; the facts are kept here so a later run that finds one does not have to re-establish them.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 300 MISSION ST → parcel 3710018; sf-parcels has blklot 3710018 active, 50–80 BEALE; the 2025 roll records it as commercial office, built 1967. EAS puts 300, 308, 310, 320 MISSION ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 300.

publish.note: Declined twice over. news/AGENTS.md: "A story about a person that mentions a building is not a building story. An obituary that names the tower someone developed belongs on no page." And the headline, which is the only text of theirs a page would carry, names a private individual and her age — the root AGENTS.md forbids that outright and there is no rewriting past it, because we do not write the entry. The feed carried this article twice under two shortlinks; both are declined here, and no source id was minted for either.
